post_text:
If an alert fires and requires no immediate human action, it is noise.

Waking an on-call engineer for a self-healing JVM transient guarantees they will eventually ignore genuine production outages.

Every un-actionable notification erodes operational discipline. Fix alert fatigue with three strict rules:

- Alert on customer-facing symptoms, not internal causes: Page on elevated HTTP 5xx rates or breached latency SLOs, not transient GC pauses or CPU blips.

- Enforce an automatic kill switch on flapping monitors: If an alert self-resolves within five minutes repeatedly, downgrade it immediately to a backlog ticket.

- Mandate an explicit mitigation runbook for every page: If the documented operational response is 'wait and see,' delete the alert definition permanently. 🚨
lesson_extracted: Alerts must trigger solely on actionable, user-facing degradation rather than transient internal metrics that self-heal.
